source.title: Dynamic Memory Based Adaptive Optimization
source.authors: B. Szegedy; Domonkos Czifra; Péter Kőrösi-Szabó

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares held-out classification accuracy for Adam and SGD across image classification tasks, using its own training setup.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports benchmark optimizer results and RLLC optimizer results. Only the Adam-versus-SGD benchmark accuracy comparisons are extracted for V4; RLLC results do not measure whether Adam generalizes worse than SGD. Training accuracy is not reported.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out optimizer and architecture comparisons. Table 1 bears on V4 and also on V3 through matched convolutional-versus-MLP comparisons, despite architecture bias not being its main research question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that RLLC can improve classical optimizers by combining them and making them adaptive, and present linear-memory variants as promising rather than establishing universal superiority. They frame the experiments as illustrative and identify larger datasets and architectures as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests its RLLC optimizers and reports benchmark Adam and SGD performance; the Adam-versus-SGD comparisons use the paper's own image-classification training setup, not a replication of the cited optimizer comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The Adam-versus-SGD accuracy ordering varies by dataset and architecture: Adam is lower only for MNIST MLP and higher in the other six settings.
record.problems: The experiments use relatively small datasets and small or medium-sized architectures. The reported table averages 3 random-seed runs; no uncertainty intervals are given in the table. The comparison does not report training performance.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the Adam-versus-SGD test-accuracy comparisons. Other optimizer results in Table 1 do not directly test V4's Adam-versus-SGD claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width variation and performance beyond the interpolation threshold.
The contribution of local connectivity separately from other architectural differences; learning sparse local connections; convolution-derived initialization of fully connected networks.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decay schedules, decoupled weight decay, and actual Adam-to-SGD switching. Training performance is not reported, so equal or better training performance cannot be established.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations for large-batch training.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.

missing.what: Matched Conv-versus-MLP accuracy and loss comparisons for each dataset under SGD, momentum SGD, and Adam. These test V3 without requiring an explicit architectural-bias intervention. Fashion-MNIST with SGD reverses the otherwise consistent convolutional advantage.

Adam-versus-SGD test-loss comparisons for all seven tasks: Adam/SGD values are 0.0758/0.0882, 0.0304/0.0331, 0.3407/0.3426, 0.2704/0.3673, 1.3858/1.4084, 0.7920/0.8359, and 0.5857/0.6010. These reveal metric dependence, especially for MNIST MLP.

Adam-versus-momentum-SGD comparisons for accuracy and loss across all seven tasks. Momentum SGD is explicitly within V4; its omission misses the near-tie on Fashion-MNIST Conv accuracy and the loss advantages for momentum SGD on CIFAR-10 Conv and ResNet-20.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Retained rows encode optimizer comparisons; V3 needs separate architecture-comparison rows rather than assigning an architecture-effect state to those optimizer contrasts. Benchmark learning rates were searched over 15 values, with no scheduler and a fixed 10,000-iteration budget. Results average three seeds; Table 1 gives no uncertainty intervals or significance tests. RLLC's interpolation between momentum SGD and SGD does not directly test Adam-to-SGD switching.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are not tested.
The paper compares architectures but does not test convolutional versus fully connected networks on the same task as a generalization-bias intervention.

No language benchmarks; no broader optimizer tuning; no decoupled weight decay or Adam-to-SGD switching; training performance is not reported, so held-out performance cannot be compared against equal or better training performance.
Batch size is fixed at 128; no large-batch comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures are not tested.
